headline: 118 Teacher-Trainers Certified After Four-Week STEAM and Inclusion Course
dek: The Ministry of Education aims to reach about 4,000 teachers by June 2027 through school-based sessions led by the new trainers.
ticker: 118 teacher-trainers certified; ministry targets 4,000 teachers by June 2027
paragraphs: The Ministry of Education on Friday handed certificates to 118 senior teachers and district methodists who finished a four-week training course at the Research Institute of Pedagogy in Talas. The course ran from 19 October to 13 November.

It covered three subjects: STEAM lessons, in which science, technology, engineering, arts and mathematics are taught through projects; teaching mixed classes that include children with disabilities and learning difficulties; and how a school plans its own small budget. Practice lessons were held at Talas Secondary School No. 31, whose headmistress, Gulmira Saparbek, opened her classrooms to the trainees.

IradOne's cameras saw one of those lessons, in which pupils combined a small robotics task with a weaving pattern. Informatics teacher Nurgul Abdykadyrova, 50, who has taught at the school since 2004, ran it. "The children do not separate the loom from the program," she said. "A pattern is a set of steps. We let them find that out with their hands first, and the visitors watched how long we wait before we explain."

Dinara Seitkulova, head of the ministry's curriculum section, said the course was built to fit the existing textbooks and thematic plans. "Nothing here asks a teacher to throw out the lesson plan," she said. "It shows how a project can sit inside one."

Each trainer will now run school-based sessions in their own district. The ministry's target is about 4,000 teachers reached by June 2027. The Iyık Janyl Pedagogical College and the Education Network of the ISEZ (iradone.com readers can find it at iradedu.org) will carry the materials to schools in the eastern districts and the Chu belt. Mukaddas Khodjaeva, a school director in Iyık Janyl, said the plan suits teachers who cannot spend weeks in Talas. "A colleague who comes to your own staff room will be heard sooner than a leaflet," she said.

Education Minister Kanykei Umotova thanked the Institute's staff and the host school, but called the course "a start, not an answer". About 1,400 teaching posts were vacant in 2025, worst for English and physics in the districts. Asked about pay, she said it is a matter for the 2027 budget.
